correctness.rationale: Formula (1) is an integral identity for the wrapped Cauchy density with the angle in (0,pi); its branch is fixed and all cells sum to one. Differentiating reciprocal arccot gives exact G-second-derivative (2), positive because 1-y arccot(y)>0 for all real y and rho>0. Three strictly ordered cosine abscissae exist iff m>=4, so the divided-difference K is positive; reciprocal conditionalized masses are affine in cosine. Symmetry of the marginalized vector forces any matching nonuniform conditionalized phase to have sin(nu)=0, hence K=0 contradiction. At m=2,3 symmetry reduces full vectors to the central mass; both P0 and Q0 are continuous strict bijections of concentration from [0,1) to [1/m,1). The sample test follows from multinomial CLT and delta method at positive fixed masses. The package checker independently integrates and tests 2814 supporting numerical assertions; no infinite claim relies on numerical enumeration.

value.rationale: The original circular-data modeling problem requires selecting between bin-integrated and point-conditionalized wrapped Cauchy likelihoods when concentration is unknown. The sharp minimal number of sectors is a natural design and identifiability invariant: at two or three bins the fitted population families coincide exactly (an impossibility boundary), while four bins guarantee population separation with an explicit computable strictly signed witness and a consistent registered-case test. This directly informs which observational resolutions can distinguish discretization mechanisms, beyond a routine comparison at equal concentrations.
